title: A case of plateau heart disease misdiagnosed as chronic pulmonary heart disease.
figures: Clubbed fingers. The end of the finger is thickened to form a clubbing bulge, and the nail is arched from the root to the end, so that the basal angle between the skin on the back of the finger tip and the nail is equal to or greater than 180 degrees.
Polycythemic face with cyanosis of lips and mouth. The skin of the face was red and the lips were purple.
Echocardiography showed enlargement of the right atrium and ventricle, mild mitral regurgitation and mild tricuspid regurgitation.
